correctness.rationale: The projector complement is a rank-two constant-diagonal projection, and its six unit-circle roots have vanishing first and second power sums, forcing a product of two cubic-binomial factors. This proves the two-orthobases configuration form, including degeneracy. The polar normal-prism/antiprism geometry gives an exhaustive vertex set; the exact facet area is 18t/(t+1)^2 by a quadrilateral diagonal cross product, and exact volume is two times the facet area by unit support and the divergence theorem. Uniform rescaling fixes each facet area to 2pi/3, giving the stated volume and sharp extrema from a derivative. The provided independent symbolic and halfspace-based checker passes, with finite checks correctly distinguished from the proof.

value.rationale: Six-node spherical two-designs form a natural minimal nontrivial continuum in the equal-facet-area Minkowski problem. Their fixed normal moments do not determine the nonlinear volume. The result provides a complete moduli classification, exact full parameter volume law, both rigid endpoint extremizers and the prism-antiprism combinatorial transition, making it a structurally motivated sharp finite-class theorem rather than a routine numerical special case.
